selections.comment: Having finished in the runner-up spot on her last two outings, compensation may beckon for CINQUE VERDE. The daughter of Sioux Nation looked to find her latest second over 5f here on the sharp side and she makes plenty of appeal reverting to 6f. Although Fine Interview failed to justify favouritism at Haydock eight days ago, it is too early to write him off. The four-year-old is feared most, ahead of the Richard Hughes-trained Knebworth.

selections.comment: Having been slowly away and staying on into second over C&D last month, STELLAR SUNRISE should have learned plenty from that opening bid. Andrew Balding's colt could prove tough to beat with that experience under his belt and appears the one to beat. The biggest threat may emerge from Poatan, who looks a likely improver stepping up in trip after his third at Beverley. Ahead Of Fashion cannot be dismissed dropping in class, while market support for newcomer River Spey would be interesting.

selections.comment: Having weakened away tamely at Wolverhampton last month, Very Mindful has something to prove at present. The application of first-time blinkers could perk the daughter of Havana Gold up and she shouldn't be underestimated judged on her previous exploits. However, CANYOUHEARTHEDRUMS hasn't been disgraced in class 2 contests of late and these calmer waters may enable a breakthrough victory. Dinamo and Miss Apres are others of interest.

selections.comment: A respectable fourth in a Group 2 contest last year, MISS TONNERRE is clear of today's rivals on official ratings. She faded away in the closing stages of the Musidora at York on last month's reappearance, but retains the potential to win at this level and Ed Walker's yard has hit top form. Anna Swan will appreciate any cut in the ground and has the ability to feature, while the Kingman filly El Budoor took a step forward when scoring at Lingfield last time and is entitled to progress again.

selections.comment: YOUTHFUL KING was beaten less than a length when runner-up over 1m6f at Salisbury. He was doing his best work in the closing stages and Luke Dace's inmate looks worth another try over this longer trip, given he was winning off today's mark last autumn. Aggagio lurks at the bottom of the handicap and he can land a blow, having placed over course and distance recently, while Spirit Mixer could shape well from the top of the weights.

selections.comment: Eight-time Group 3 winner Hamish justified favouritism in a Listed contest when last seen and makes his return to action. The nine-year-old will be hoping for as much rain as possible and sets the standard with an official rating of 117, but the vote goes to BOLSTER. Karl Burke's charge struck in this class at Newmarket on his final start last season and was pestered on the lead when fourth in the Huxley at Chester last month. He hasn't hit his ceiling yet and could take a step forward to score. Last year's German Derby winner Palladium completes the shortlist on his debut for the Gosdens.

selections.comment: Racingbreaks Ryder outran his odds of 33/1 to make the frame at Kempton last month and, with all five of his career victories coming on turf, he has to be respected. Rey De La Batalla could only manage sixth over C&D last time but takes a drop in grade and is one to watch. However, NARIKO was beaten by the smallest of margins into second at Doncaster when last seen and is just 2lb higher on her return to the fray. With a similar performance, she could be the one to beat.

Riaan took the silver medal home in a Grade 3 handicap at the Punchestown Festival and commands the utmost respect for the Gordon Elliott team. Young Buster looks best of the rest.

Gary Rutherford's charge is feared most, ahead of Donso Star.

selections.comment: Happy Index notched a fourth victory over hurdles when landing the spoils here last month and she's sure to prove popular in her follow-up bid. However, Olly Murphy's mare could be worth taking on off a career-high mark with TRUE DESTINY. The veteran arrives on the back of a solid third at Downpatrick and he may prove slightly better handicapped raiding these shores. Kelso scorer Our Girl Sal completes the shortlist.

selections.comment: This looks a golden opportunity for SPANISH HARLEM. While yet to win over fences, the chestnut seven-year-old is a battle-hardened handicapper and was an excellent fourth in the bet365 Gold Cup at Sandown in April. Off a mark of 139 and with Sean Cleary-Farrell claiming 7lb, the Willie Mullins-trained French bred is difficult to oppose. Successful on his debut over the larger obstacles at Down Royal last month, Baltic Bird is an obvious danger, while No Time To Wait (first-time cheekpieces) is another that warrants respect. Minella Sergeant and Ballinrea complete the line-up and both are likely to struggle.

selections.comment: The subject of good market support over C&D last month, LISNAGAR FORTUNE was ultimately let down by his jumping. Making numerous errors on his way around, the Soldier Of Fortune seven-year-old still did very well to finish a never-nearer third. Already twice a winner at this venue, the 127-rated bay should prove hard to beat if getting his jumping in order. A Grade 2 winner when in the care of Harry Fry, it'll be interesting to see how In Excelsis Deo fares on his debut for Enda Bolger, while handicap debutant Antrim Coast and six-time winner Grange Walk are others for the shortlist.

selections.comment: The 92-rated ROSE BOUM is the suggestion in this competitive affair. With Hannah Phillips claiming 7lb, the Paul Nolan-trained five-year-old will carry a featherweight. Second and beaten by just a length-and-a-quarter when last seen at Wexford, she encouragingly drew 25 lengths clear of the third. Already twice successful from four track starts, top-weight Locked Box is an obvious danger with Georgie Benson aboard, while it'll be interesting to see how Tullyveery Lad fares on his return from a break. In truth, a case can be made for many others, with Downpatrick winner Queenofthelodge, the Jody Townend-ridden Your Honour and Des McDonogh's In For The Night, all sure to have plenty of supporters.

selections.comment: KEEP UP could make a winning transition to hurdling. She was a comfortable winner of a bumper at Roscommon last summer and then was deemed good enough to contest a Listed mares' bumper at Gowran Park in which she finished fifth. Willie Mullins and jockey Sean Cleary-Farrell teamed up to land this race last year. Gordon Elliott runs two horses with Fillusin reappearing after a campaign that saw her placed in four maiden hurdles, while newcomer Milesfromthehonk is a full-sister to a double winner over fences. Regards To Rose has been placed in her last two maiden hurdles and is race fit, so has stronger claims than most of her rivals. Point-to-point winner Kilrush Lady is worth a market check.

selections.comment: This step up in trip may see JOLI TRAVAIL to better effect after keeping on at one pace for third over an extended 2m4f in Killarney. Anna McGuinness is getting opportunities for Willie Mullins and rode a winner for the stable at Kilbeggan last weekend. Gordon Elliott's Jazz De Cotte is also up in trip, but has a bit more experience and cheekpieces are tried after a runner-up berth in Downpatrick. His stablemate William Butler has had the benefit of racing over a longer trip when fifth at Limerick and third in Tipperary, so should have a role to play. Sporting Glance and Mister Frostie aren't out of contention, while Ludovico Sforza is a point-to-point winner to note.

selections.comment: Dual course winner LONDONOFFICECALLIN stayed on strongly to the line at Ballinrobe last time and looks capable of striking back here, despite a 2lb rise. He didn't get the clearest run around and was doing his best work late on. Westernersunrise has had a little break since winning well at Fairyhouse back in February. A 6lb rise doesn't look harsh, but she may appreciate some rain. Howdoyalikeherhome has been running consistently well and is another who has to come into calculations.

selections.comment: LUKER'S TIPPLE sets a good standard here off 122 and should prove the one to beat. On his last run over timber he finished mid-division in the Fred Winter at Cheltenham and ran a big race on the level at Bellewstown on his last outing when losing out by a neck to one of today's rivals Mick Collins. The latter was beaten favourite on his hurdling debut at Cork last month but it wasn't a bad run to finish fifth and he's entitled to improve a bit from the experience. Watching The Clock ran a nice race on her debut when third in Tipperary and, with that run under her belt, she could be a big player now.

selections.comment: Plenty in this field have questions to answer regarding soft ground. CANYOUHEARTHEDRUMS drops back in trip to five furlongs after a below-par effort at Windsor last time out and arguably sets the standard based on her second at Bath over the minimum trip on debut. Very Mindful has twice filled the runner-up spot and could bounce back with first-time blinkers on for first turf start if handling the conditions. Sayidah Poets has yet to seriously feature but her best run came over this C&D two starts ago and she could figure if building on that.

selections.comment: HAMISH ended last season with a commanding 5l win in the Finale Stakes (Listed) at the Curragh and, as a five-time Group 3 winner who relishes a sharp track, he’s the pick on balance of form. Military Academy signed off 2024 with a Listed success on the AW and ran respectably in Bahrain’s King’s Cup in March; with his yard in form, he looks a solid value option. Bolster has enjoyed a productive 2024 with four wins and wasn’t disgraced when fourth in the Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester, though he has a bit to prove stepping up in trip.

selections.comment: Statuario took this contest last year off 2lb lower and is closely matched fellow veteran Annsam on their recent meeting here. The pair were beaten by a progressive rival that day and have dropped to very attractive marks so ought to go close. However the pair may be vulnerable to the unexposed BALLINTUBBER BOY who is yet to win over fences but was only out-battled late last time by a well handicapped rival. The form of his debut runner up effort has been franked emphatically and he is open to plenty of improvement now handicapping so he gets the verdict in an open race.

He's been highly tried in handicaps and can take advantage of a class and experience edge here. No Time To Wait was let down by his jumping last time at Cheltenham but had shaped with promise behind some useful sorts previously. He could be the biggest threat ahead of Baltic Bird who made a winning chase debut but will find this tougher.

He looks well treated on his first couple of chase starts behind future Grade 1 winners and can make a winning handicap debut. Antrim Coast is yet to match his hurdles form over fences but was backed as if capable of better last time and should be competitive on handicap debut if getting a stiff test. Veteran Grange Walk proved he retained his ability over hurdles in the spring and was given too much to do last time. He could run into a place.

selections.comment: Philip Rothwell holds a strong hand here and it's the unexposed HARRY'S DREAM who appeals most. He was far from disgraced on handicap debut having gone off too quickly and the form of his debut runner up effort has been franked. If the tongue tie brings any improvement he can account for consistent stablemate Warm In Gorey who will appreciate this step back up in trip. Recent winner Queenofthelodge has seen her form franked and will also remain competitive off this revised mark.

selections.comment: STAY GOLD has proven a touch frustrating but he has caught the eye on a number of occasions and looks on a competitive mark. He flew home from an impossible position last time suggesting that he could shed his maiden tag now upped to 3m. One And Only was placed when returned to handicaps last time having produced a big effort before falling in a hot novice previously. He is entitled to be competitive once more whilst dual purpose performer Londonofficecallin is another arriving in form who will relish this step up in trip. He completes the list of dangers.

selections.comment: LUKER'S TIPPLE sets a clear standard on his Listed spill when he would've placed and his solid midfield effort in the Fred Winter. He's had a solid run on the flat since to keep up his fitness and should be outclassing these. Mick Collins was a winner in the other code over the spring and though he's yet to deliver on that promise over hurdles he could prove the biggest threat. It was a weak race which Watching The Clock placed in on debut but this isn't much stronger and a replication of that effort could see her fill the same position.
